title: COSH evaluates (EXP(x) + EXP(-x))/2 via stored x87 addition, returning #NUM! above ln(DBL_MAX) where cosh(x) is still finite
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, COSH(x) computes RN53(RN64(EXP(x) + EXP(-x))) / 2 using Excel's worksheet EXP kernel rather than calling the Windows CRT cosh() (which differs by 1 ULP on 29 of 1,224 W111 extended-numeric rows, and at 0.001, 0.01, and 10). Because EXP(|x|) overflows binary64 around 709.7827, COSH(-709.7827128933891) returns #NUM! even though the mathematical cosh is ~8.98846567435735e+307, half of DBL_MAX. All 33,550 full-bank COSH rows match.
basis: Measured across Excel 16.0 build 20430 extended-numeric and integer-hyperbolic held-out captures in CalcFunc-Evidence and matched on 33,550/33,550 full-bank COSH rows.

correct.how: cosh(|-709.7827128933891|) = (exp(|x|) + exp(-|x|))/2 computed at 120 decimal digits in Python Decimal and rounded to nearest binary64.
